pull.title: KAFKA-16020: Use elapsed time comparison in waitForFuture to avoid nanoTime overflow
pull.body:
### Problem
Time#waitForFuture compares absolute nanoTime values directly (`deadlineNs <= nowNs` and `deadlineNs - nowNs`). As noted in the JDK docs for System.nanoTime(), comparing absolute nanoTimes is unsafe due to potential overflow (wrap-around).

### Solution
Compare elapsed time instead: compute `startTimeNs = nanoseconds()` and use `elapsedNs = nowNs - startTimeNs` vs `timeoutNs = deadlineNs - startTimeNs`. This correctly handles nanoTime overflow.

### Testing
- Compiled clients module successfully.
- This is a minimal, safe fix following JDK recommendation. Additional unit tests could be added, but the existing behavior is preserved.

commit.message:
KAFKA-19022: Log the compared cluster ids on INCONSISTENT_CLUSTER_ID

When a raft request carries a cluster id that does not match the local
cluster id, the client rejects it with INCONSISTENT_CLUSTER_ID but the
two ids being compared are never surfaced, so it is impossible to tell
from the logs whether the local id or the incoming id is wrong.

Log both ids when the mismatch is detected in hasValidClusterId,
covering every request type (Vote, BeginQuorumEpoch, EndQuorumEpoch,
Fetch, FetchSnapshot, AddRaftVoter, RemoveRaftVoter, UpdateRaftVoter).
This is a diagnostics-only change: no wire protocol or response schema
is modified, so no KIP is required.

Also allow org.apache.logging.log4j.Level in the raft test sources so
the new test can assert the log output, matching the existing
allow-lists for other modules.
